locations: the cosmos seen within Krishna’s mouth
continuity.narrative_arc: Yashoda’s ordinary maternal care meets Krishna’s cosmic form: the child yawns, plays, is accused of eating earth, denies it, reveals worlds within his mouth, and returns to her lap.
continuity.reference_mapping: Captain-supplied readiness record maps 001.jpg–010.jpg sequentially to canonical stanzas 1–10. Tamil text pages 011.jpg and 012.jpg remain excluded.
continuity.source_text: Canonical Sanskrit and IAST follow Stotra Nidhi Dasakam 46. Caption commentary is retained verbatim and is not canonical translation.
continuity.palette_arc: Matte mineral ochre, maroon, warm cream and muted foliage; Krishna uses deep indigo-blue skin. Cosmic scenes remain painterly and restrained, not glossy or photorealistic.
continuity.batch_selection: Ten landscape-only candidates are intended for an unapproved reference-versus-candidate review chapter. This plan does not approve artwork. Portraits remain paused.

must_show: Yashoda cradles the nursing-age infant Krishna safely across her lap after feeding.
The infant yawns; a tiny but legible universe appears within the open mouth, with no separate panel.
Keep Krishna an infant with exactly two ordinary external arms and legs in this human scene; no exposed nursing.
scene_brief.composition: Intimate horizontal lap scene, faces and the small mouth cosmos in clear view.

stanzas.alt: Yashoda holds the infant Krishna as a universe appears in his yawn.
stanzas.reference_guidance: Photo 001 sets only the lap and yawn moment; infant anchor sets Krishna identity; the D043 source sets Yashoda identity; D001 images set style. Recompose for 16:9.

must_show: Krishna sits with two distinct young cowherd boys in a fruit grove after eating the fruit he promised to share.
One boy brings the complaint to Yashoda and gestures back toward Krishna; the other stands with the fruit pile, visibly upset.
All three children have complete modest village clothing, distinct faces, and naturally attached two-arm and two-leg anatomy; Krishna follows his shared youthful Vraja contract.
scene_brief.composition: A single grove scene: Krishna beside shared fruit at right, Yashoda seated at left, and two boys between them, one complaining to her.
scene_brief.tone: Playful mischief followed by a child’s complaint.

stanzas.alt: Two cowherd boys tell Yashoda that Krishna ate the fruit he had promised to share.
stanzas.reference_guidance: Photo 002 guides the fruit grove and cowherd boys. Use the Krishna reference for identity only, the D043 source for Yashoda identity only, and D001 for rendering. Recompose for 16:9.

must_show: Yashoda is alarmed that the child may become ill after eating earth, while Krishna calmly sits before her.
Suggest the cosmic truth that Krishna consumes earth and waters at pralaya through a restrained reflection within the mouth or a small cosmic motif integrated into the scene.
Show Yashoda’s loving concern without making her aware of Krishna’s divinity; two external arms per human figure.
scene_brief.composition: Close domestic exchange with child, mother, and a quiet cosmic-earth detail integrated into one frame.
scene_brief.tone: Maternal concern with hidden cosmic scale.

stanzas.alt: Yashoda worries that Krishna has eaten earth, unaware of his cosmic nature.
stanzas.reference_guidance: Photo 003 guides the mother-child exchange; use the two identity anchors only for identity and D001 for the matte style. Recompose for 16:9.

must_show: Yashoda repeatedly asks Krishna whether he ate mud, leaning toward him with a questioning gesture.
Krishna smiles and firmly denies it, with clean lips and face and no earth visible in the scene.
Keep both figures naturally attached and two-armed; Krishna’s forehead is plain and unmarked.
scene_brief.composition: A close, balanced two-person exchange with clear gestures and expressive faces.

stanzas.alt: Yashoda questions Krishna, who smiles and denies eating mud.
stanzas.reference_guidance: Photo 004 provides the exact gesture and moment. D001 are style references; the two identity cues guide faces only. Recompose for 16:9.

must_show: Yashoda tells Krishna that others have confirmed the accusation and asks him to open his mouth.
Krishna begins opening his mouth slowly, like a lotus unfolding; keep the mouth human-sized and do not yet show a cosmic tableau.
Both figures remain fully clothed with ordinary attached limbs; Krishna’s forehead is bare.
scene_brief.composition: Mother’s prompting gesture and the child beginning to open his mouth are the clear focal point.

stanzas.alt: Krishna begins to open his mouth at Yashoda’s request.
stanzas.reference_guidance: Photo 005 controls the slow opening-mouth moment. Identity anchors guide faces only; D001 images guide style. Recompose for 16:9.

must_show: Yashoda looks into Krishna’s small open mouth and sees the entire earth and universe, not mud alone.
Include an integrated small worldscape with earth, sky and waters inside the mouth, clearly contained within the child’s face.
Krishna’s external form remains youthful and two-armed, with bare forehead; use no light beams or detached cosmic panel.
scene_brief.composition: Keep both faces and the mouth-contained universe clearly readable in a single horizontal scene.

stanzas.alt: Yashoda sees the whole universe inside Krishna’s open mouth.
stanzas.reference_guidance: Photo 006 guides the complete cosmos-in-mouth vision. Keep the universe inside the mouth, not a detached panel. Identity and style references are not pose references.

must_show: Inside Krishna’s mouth, show forest, ocean, clouds, sky and Rasatala as distinct regions of one contained cosmos.
Show tiny humans, asuras and devas in their respective regions; they are inhabitants within the vision, not extra external people.
Keep Krishna’s face and Yashoda’s astonished gaze clear; external Krishna has two arms and bare forehead.
scene_brief.composition: One close mother-child scene, with a single contained mouth cosmos organized into readable horizontal world bands.

stanzas.alt: Yashoda sees forests, oceans, skies, Rasatala, humans, asuras and devas within Krishna’s mouth.
stanzas.reference_guidance: Photo 007 is the exact contents reference for the mouth-world. The two D001 images set rendering; identity images guide faces only. Recompose for 16:9.

landscape.candidate_status: Selected landscape v008, SHA-256 9b69d43c1dc60d9fe246357de230f8591cb384cd96fd54672a681b53f8e21dad. Producer inspected the native frame and enlarged Yashoda face, open hand, visible feet and mouth-world details; the mother and child remain distinct with attached limbs, and the forest, ocean, cloud, sky and Rasatala bands remain separate with tiny witnesses inside the mouth. Yashoda’s open hand shows a thumb plus four fingers; her visible foot and both visible Krishna feet each show five toes. Yashoda cheek patch (650,250) RGB (197,117,79), R-B 118; outer Krishna cheek (1150,175) RGB (19,78,226), B-R 207. Tiny inner witness digits cannot be certified individually. DISCLOSED DEVIATION: after three color-repair attempts (v006, v007, v008), 4x4 skin-only patch R-B medians are deva face 127, deva arm 100, asura arm 129 (v008); the asura readings for v006/v007/v008 are 135/130/129, so the last remains above the approximately 120 warm-brown target. Firstmate accepted this measured range as still reading warm tan-brown for the tiny figures. Independent exact-checksum review pending; art remains unapproved.

must_show: Yashoda sees Hari reclining upon Adishesha over the milk ocean within the child’s open mouth.
Show the reclining divine form and serpent couch only as a miniature contained vision inside Krishna’s mouth; the outer child remains two-armed.
Yashoda sees both the cosmic form and the child before her; keep those nested levels distinct and legible.
scene_brief.composition: A balanced outer mother-child scene with a small but clear reclining Vishnu in the mouth-contained vision.

stanzas.alt: Within Krishna’s mouth, Yashoda sees Hari reclining on Adishesha over the milk ocean.
stanzas.reference_guidance: Photo 008 depicts the reclining Vaikuntha vision; it is scene context only. Follow Vishnu and Adishesha contracts for divine attributes, while the outer child stays under the Krishna contract.

landscape.candidate_status: Selected landscape v008, SHA-256 65dab0078c54ab0119dea8f15c76c292655f65baed33aea8dbbb3e54612f1592. Producer inspected the native frame and enlarged Yashoda hand/feet, outer Krishna face, and contained Hari views. Yashoda cheek patch (650,250) RGB (134,87,64), R-B 70; outer Krishna cheek (1150,175) RGB (33,80,208), B-R 175. Hari’s 4x4 skin-only medians are face (1080,370) RGB (40,74,196), B-R 156; exposed arm (1117,390) RGB (46,79,190), B-R 144; second exposed arm (1150,395) RGB (15,58,125), B-R 110. Yashoda’s open hand shows a thumb plus four fingers; visible feet each show five toes. No additional outer limbs, duplicates, text, border or watermark observed. Independent exact-checksum review pending; art remains unapproved.

must_show: A world appears within Krishna’s mouth; inside that world Yashoda sees Krishna opening his mouth again, with another smaller world repeating toward infinity.
Make the nesting explicitly intentional with two or three progressively smaller mother-child layers; one outer pair remains full-sized.
Preserve Krishna’s plain forehead and ordinary two-arm outer anatomy; nested figures are tiny world images.
scene_brief.composition: Single coherent recursive cosmos centered inside Krishna’s mouth, no separate panel.

stanzas.alt: Yashoda sees the worlds repeating within Krishna’s mouth, receding toward infinity.
stanzas.reference_guidance: Photo 009 guides the recursively nested world. Keep all repetition inside the mouth as deliberate miniatures; identity and style references guide only their stated roles.

must_show: After a brief recognition of Krishna’s divinity, Yashoda holds him tenderly on her lap as her child again.
Krishna reaches affectionately toward her, asking to be fed; communicate this through the embrace and a nearby covered feeding bowl without depicting nursing.
Keep Yashoda’s clothing opaque and complete, Krishna’s forehead bare and his external anatomy naturally two-armed.
scene_brief.composition: Warm horizontal lap scene with a return from cosmic awe to maternal affection.

stanzas.alt: Krishna returns to Yashoda’s lap as her affectionate child.
stanzas.reference_guidance: Photo 010 guides the mother-child embrace. The scene does not show nursing; clothing remains complete. Identity anchors guide identity only and D001 anchors guide style.
